reviews.title: Used to be amazing
reviews.text:
I used to use the app about six months ago, and it worked perfectly. Now, every time I open the app, I’m forced to create a new account and sign in again, which is extremely frustrating.

On top of that, the app won’t let me block more than three apps at a time, even though I paid for a full year of the One Sec subscription. At this point, the subscription feels like a complete waste of money because I’m paying for features that either don’t work properly or that I can’t even use.

I really liked the app before, so it’s disappointing to see it become this difficult to use. I’d appreciate it if these issues could be fixed or if someone could explain why my paid subscription isn’t working as expected.

reviews.title: Privacy Concerns
reviews.text: I used this app for a year back in 2023 and then never used it again but it sat in my phone since then. I recently (as in July 2026) was saving a page on safari to my reading lists and one of the options was “Add to onesec’s reading list”. I am honestly baffled at why onesec would even have a reading list to begin with. It’s an app to lower screen time. I never created a reading list for this app nor did I give it permission to create one. Zero stars if I could.

reviews.title: Strong blocking, but missing real accountability
reviews.text:
This app does a good job enforcing Screen Time limits, but it falls short as an accountability tool.

Like most Screen Time apps, it relies on three mechanisms:
	•	app time limits
	•	unlocks / temporary access
	•	scheduled blocks

The problem is that following or breaking these rules isn’t meaningfully tracked. Users can:
	•	repeatedly use unlocks
	•	change limits or schedules after enforcement starts
	•	revoke Screen Time permissions and re-enable later

…without any persistent history or consequence inside the app. That makes it easy to undermine your own rules quietly, which defeats the purpose for serious users.

What would make this a 5-star app:
	•	an accountability history (unlock usage, schedule adherence, rule changes)
	•	logging Screen Time permission revocations/restores
	•	an integrity metric (did I keep my word or not)
	•	brief, optional reflection prompts at key moments (before unlocks, after rule changes)
	•	weekly summaries focused on accountability, not just usage minutes
	•	a place to define and revisit why you’re limiting apps, so behavior change is internal, not just enforced

Blocking alone changes behavior temporarily.
Accountability, integrity tracking, and reflection change it long-term.

If these additions were made, this would easily be a 5-star app.
